## AccountRepository

*class*

All SQL for the household, app_user and household_member tables lives here.
The rest of the app never writes SQL against the database; it calls these methods.

The insert methods run on a caller-supplied connection (see .openTransaction()) so the
service can create a household, its first user and the membership linking them atomically.

## AccountSelfService

*class*

What a logged-in user may do to their own account: change the email and the password. Both need the current password,
and a wrong one counts as a login attempt from that client address (LoginThrottle), so a stolen session cannot
be used to guess it. No SQL here, no UI here.

## AccountService

*class*

Business logic for user accounts and households. No SQL here, no UI here.

Passwords only ever pass through here on their way into the PasswordEncoder (BCrypt in
the app); only the resulting hash is handed to the repository. Emails are trimmed and lower-cased
before they are stored or looked up, so "Anna@Example.de" and "anna@example.de" are one account.

There is deliberately no public sign-up: accounts are created by the operator through
UserAdminRunner. For now there is a single shared household: the first user creates it
(as HouseholdRole.ADMIN), everyone after joins it as HouseholdRole.MEMBER.

## InvitationService

*class*

Invitations into a household: an admin makes one, the code is shown ONCE, and whoever enters it (with an email, a name and
a password) becomes a HouseholdRole.MEMBER of that household. There is no open sign-up: without a valid code nobody
can make an account.

The code is 16 characters from an alphabet of 32 without look-alikes (80 bits), shown as XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX. Only its
SHA-256 is stored. An invitation works once, for #VALID_DAYS days, and an admin can revoke it. Entering a code
counts as an attempt of the client address (LoginThrottle, the same slow-down as a login); a right code gives
the attempt back. No SQL here, no UI here.

## LoginThrottle

*class*

A delay that grows with login attempts from one client address, not a lockout. The attempt is counted BEFORE the
password is looked at (so many attempts sent at the same moment cannot all slip through while the first is still being
checked): the first #THRESHOLD attempts are allowed, the next ones are refused for 30 seconds, then 60, 120 ...
up to 15 minutes. A correct password gives its own attempt back. Attempts are forgotten after an hour without one.

There is deliberately no limit per email: such a limit lets anybody who knows an email address keep the real user
out by guessing wrong once in a while. Guessing spread over many addresses is for the edge (Cloudflare) to stop.
In memory: a restart clears it. Thread-safe (one lock; the work under it is tiny, the password check is outside).

```mermaid
classDiagram
    direction LR
    class auth_LoginThrottle["LoginThrottle"] {
        +int THRESHOLD$
        -long SECOND$
        -long BASE_COOLDOWN$
        -long MAX_COOLDOWN$
        -long FORGET_AFTER$
        -int MAX_ENTRIES$
        -Map~String, Entry~ byIp
        -LongSupplier nanoClock
        +LoginThrottle(LongSupplier nanoClock)
        +begin(String ip) OptionalLong
        +succeeded(String ip) void
    }
    class auth_LoginThrottle_Entry["LoginThrottle.Entry"]
    class auth_AccountSelfService["AccountSelfService"]
    class auth_InvitationService["InvitationService"]

        <<spring>>
    }

    api_ServiceConfig ..> auth_LoginThrottle

    auth_InvitationService --> auth_LoginThrottle
    auth_LoginService --> auth_LoginThrottle
```

## UserAdminRunner

*class · command-line tool*

Command-line entry point for managing logins. DAHÄM is self-hosted, so there is no public
sign-up endpoint: the operator creates the accounts on the server. Run it from the app directory
(the one containing data/), against the same database the API uses:

  create-user   [householdName]
      The first user creates the household (default name "DAHÄM") and becomes its ADMIN;
      later users join that household as MEMBER.
  create-household-user
      Starts a NEW household with this user as its ADMIN, even if households exist (a second household). Everyone else
      joins it by invitation (the admin makes one in the app).
  set-password
      Sets a new password for an existing user (there are no password-reset emails).

The password is read from the DAHAEM_PASSWORD environment variable if it is set (for scripted
setups), otherwise prompted for twice on the console without echo. It is never taken as an
argument, so it does not end up in shell history or the process list.

Exit code: 0 = OK, 1 = failed, 2 = bad arguments.

```mermaid
    direction LR

        +main(String[] args) void$
    }
```
